clue.text: Foreign currency in volume can be a worry

indicators.note: the currency is placed inside the word for a volume, so in tells us one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a tome is a large book, a volume
roubles are the money of Russia, a foreign currency to British readers

explanation.surface: Dealing in foreign money while holding a big book is a source of anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bothersome that causes anxiety is a worry; the adjective describes such a cause.

clue.text: End of river, by the mouth, is dewy

indicators.note: end of picks out the closing letter of the word river

parts.note: oral means taken by the mouth

explanation.surface: At a river's estuary the ground is wet with dew.
explanation.definitionFit: Roral is a rare poetic adjective meaning covered with or like dew, from Latin ros, dew.

clue.text: Opening means ruin!

explanation.surface: An opening, the clue proclaims, spells ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfastening a knot or button is an opening action; a person's downfall or ruin is also called that word.

clue.text: Boat used for towing?

explanation.surface: A vessel employed to tow others.
explanation.definitionFit: A two- or three-masted sailing vessel with lugsails has this name; whimsically, something that lugs or drags a load is one too.

clue.text: Take on board measure for repairs

parts.note: to ship is to take aboard a vessel
a yard is an imperial measure of length

explanation.surface: Loading a measuring rule onto a vessel needing repair.
explanation.definitionFit: Boats are built and mended at this waterside works, a place for repairs.

clue.text: Most timid fictional bird in muster

indicators.note: the bird is placed inside the gathering, so in signals one piece within another

parts.note: a meet is a gathering, a muster
Kes is the kestrel in Barry Hines's novel A Kestrel for a Knave, filmed as Kes

explanation.surface: The shyest storybook bird at an assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: Kes is the 1969 Ken Loach film of Barry Hines's novel about a boy and his kestrel, so the fictional bird is its title; 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Meek means submissive and mild, so the superlative is the most timid.

clue.text: A permanent gas given off by such chemical salts

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are let loose and rearranged, as a gas given off disperses

explanation.surface: A gas that lasts is released by certain chemical compounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given off' is the anagram signal on A PERMANENT GAS, which rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Salts of permanganic acid, such as potassium permanganate, are a family of chemical salts.

clue.text: Sheds light where river runs through underground passage

indicators.note: the river letter flows through the middle of the passage, placed inside it

parts.note: a pothole is a deep cave or shaft underground

explanation.surface: A stream flowing through a cave lets light in.
explanation.definitionFit: A round window in a ship's side admits light into the cabin.

clue.text: Once the cheapest means of transport?

definitions.text: Once the cheapest means of transport?

parts.words: Once the cheapest means of transport?
parts.note: a Victorian bicycle named after two small old coins, as if it cost almost nothing

explanation.surface: Asking what used to be the least expensive way to travel.
explanation.walkthrough: A penny and a farthing were small pre-decimal British coins; the old high-wheeled bicycle was named after them.
explanation.definitionFit: The high-wheeler bicycle of the 1870s carried two coin names, making it sound the cheapest vehicle.

clue.text: Strayed right among wild deer

indicators.note: the letter for right is placed among the rearranged letters
wild suggests the letters of deer running loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A wanderer went right in among untamed deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges DEER into ERED; 'among' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander from the correct path, which is to go wrong or make a mistake.

clue.text: I grope, due to this having been taken off?

definitions.text: I grope, due to this having been taken off?

indicators.note: taken off suggests a rope removed and its letters thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone fumbles because the line guiding them has been removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been taken off' is the anagram signal: I GROPE, DUE rearranges to the answer, and the whole clue says why you would grope without one.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope used to steer or steady something, such as a balloon's trailing line, helps one feel the way.

clue.text: Headgear of factory in East, on the railway

parts.note: a mill is a factory
RY is a standard abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Hats made at a works out east beside the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Hats and the trade of making them for women are collectively called by this term.

clue.text: Taken down during board meeting

parts.note: board here means meals, so food swallowed at mealtime, not minutes recorded at a company gathering

explanation.surface: Notes recorded in a company's directors' meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken down' suggests minutes written up; 'board' is bed-and-board, meals, so it is food swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Food consumed or swallowed is taken down the throat at a meal.

clue.text: For example, girl holds nothing back? It's her immaturity

indicators.note: back means the whole assembled string is read in reverse order
the girl's name contains the letter for nothing

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A girl, for instance, holds back nothing because she is still young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole assembled string round, not just the girl's name; 'her' links the immaturity to the girl of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Being legally under age, a minor's youth, is a state of immaturity.

clue.text: Hunt chat — turn around and there's another bird!

indicators.note: turn around tells us the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chat is a bird; hunt it, then spin round and see a different bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn around' could suggest a reversal, but it is an anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tree-climbing songbird of the family Sittidae; chat in the clue is also a bird, hence another.

clue.text: Send a letter -it's damaged beyond repair

explanation.surface: Posting a note about something wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch correspondence is to pen and post it; a vehicle not worth mending is a total loss in insurance terms.

clue.text: Lock secures the spring from encroachment

indicators.note: the lock of hair holds the spring safely inside it

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A lock keeps the spring safe from intruders.
explanation.definitionFit: Entering another's land unlawfully is an encroachment on it.

clue.text: Playing sitar, attempt finale, to reveal expertise

indicators.note: finale puts the attempt at the very end of the answer
playing suggests the letters of sitar are performed in a new order

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Performing a sitar piece and trying a big finish shows real skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finale' is a positional signal: the attempt comes last, after the rearranged instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistic skill and craftsmanship is expertise.

clue.text: Ask Mimi round to see the plant

indicators.note: round suggests the letters turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Invite Mimi over to view a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like an invitation to visit, but it signals an anagram of ASK MIMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimmia is an evergreen shrub with red berries, a garden plant.

clue.text: Earned enough, in a way, to inspire affection

indicators.note: in a way hints that the letters are taken in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Making enough money in some fashion wins people's fondness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' signals the anagram of EARNED; 'enough' is padding to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone loved or liked is to inspire affection in others.

clue.text: This egg will have three points — face up to it

parts.note: N, E and W are three compass points

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read from the bottom, reversed

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock

explanation.surface: An egg with three tips: confront it bravely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses DIAL to LAID in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshly produced egg straight from the hen is described this way.

clue.text: Noxious stuff I spoon out

indicators.note: out tells us the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone spooning out a harmful substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxic substance is noxious stuff.

clue.text: Violin producing a lustreless finish, I concluded

indicators.note: concluded puts the letter I at the close of the word

parts.note: a mat or matt finish is dull, lacking shine

explanation.surface: A violinmaker produces a dull final coat and decides it is done.
explanation.walkthrough: AMATI was a famous family of violin makers in Cremona; their instruments bear the name.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument made by the Cremona family of luthiers is called after them, as a Stradivarius is.

clue.text: Stay on guard! in this case every second counts

definitions.text: in this case every second counts

parts.note: to stop is to stay or remain
a watch is a guard or sentry

explanation.surface: A sentry ordered to stay alert where every second matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A timing device for races, measuring elapsed seconds, comes in a watch case.

clue.text: Awfully hot -— no good for beachwear

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of hot are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: It is terribly hot and swimwear is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A skimpy swimsuit or sandal worn at the seaside is beachwear.

clue.text: Snaps come out and go round

indicators.note: out suggests the letters come out of their order

explanation.surface: Photographs emerge and are passed around.
explanation.definitionFit: To surround or encircle something is to go round it.

clue.text: Trouble the sailors found on deck

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for the sailors

explanation.surface: A disturbance among seamen on the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' is a verb meaning decorate, not a ship's floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to decorate, the verb meaning embellish.

clue.text: Animals going to earth when there's a cloudburst

explanation.surface: Pets run for cover in a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: Two common household pets, and the idiom raining heavily; both senses use the pair of pet names.
